summary.intent: Fix a visual bug in the file upload progress bar where the bar flashes full-width before snapping back to 0% when transitioning from encrypting to uploading state.
summary.outcome: Identified the root cause (CSS `width: 100% !important` in pulse animation conflicting with inline progress style) and fixed it by replacing the full-width pulse with a shimmer animation in upload.css.

repo: Upload progress is handled via useDropUpload.ts hook with onFileProgress/uploadFiles callbacks from a batch pipeline SDK
Upload states include at least 'encrypting' and 'uploading', each with distinct CSS treatments
upload.css uses a pulse class with !important width override to fake 100% during encrypting state

code.finding: Pulse animation used width: 100% !important, which conflicts with inline style width set by first progress event, causing a visible flash/snap when transitioning to uploading state
Progress events fire rapidly from the batch pipeline SDK; first event resets width to 0% via inline style after pulse class is removed

workflow: Grepping for event handler names (onFileProgress, uploadFiles) is an effective way to trace progress update flow through SDK integrations

friction: The !important override in the pulse class made the CSS interaction non-obvious — inline styles normally take precedence, but !important reversed that, masking the bug source
